steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper on optimal adversarial attacks in multi-agent reinforcement learning where the attackers are themselves agents with limited budgets. Motivate the problem, review prior attack work, state what we propose, and close with how the paper is organized.

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Reinforcement learning (RL), and also multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), is the algorithm used underneath for agents that interact with a dynamic environment and make decisions in it. In MARL there are multiple players (agents) that interact with the environment, and the environment dynamics depend on the joint actions of all of the agents. Researchers usually assume that MARL is a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and that the game model is a Markov game (MG). RL is used in a lot of different scenarios, for example autonomous driving, financial decisions, recommendation systems, and drones' and robots' algorithms. RL models, MARL included, are being used more and more in critical tasks, so understanding the security and adversarial robustness of RL and MARL is becoming more important.

Some recent works have looked at adversarial attacks on single-agent RL. In general there are 5 types of adversarial attacks: observation poisoning attacks, environment poisoning attacks, action-only poisoning attacks, reward-only poisoning attacks, and mixed poisoning attacks. For example, one work investigated the optimality of evasion attacks (attacks that reduce the expected total reward the agents gain) under a budget constraint, looking at it from the perspective of policy perturbations during learning. Another work proposed two types of attacks, the strategically-timed attack and the enchanting attack, where the attacker wants to lure the victim (recipient) agent into a designated target state.

- MARL setting
  - most existing works: one limitless attacker attacking multiple agents
  - mediator model: generalized mediator's objective; mediator (attacker) attacks agents to mediate them to maximize objective function in an MG
  - adversarial attacks on communication of multi-agent systems
  - mediator work assumes one limitless mediator (attacker) attacking recipient agents
  - reality: attacks by distributed agents; each attacker has budget constraint on resources
- Our proposal
  - agent-attack-agent model: distributed agents instead of central mediators; distinct cost per attacker-recipient pair; own budget per attacker
  - optimal method: within-step static constrained attack-resource allocation optimization + between-step dynamic programming
  - numerical results: attacks significantly reduce rewards of attacked agents
- Organization
  - Section 2: model and problem formulation
  - Section 3: two budget constraint scenarios, two optimal algorithms
  - Section 4: numerical evaluation

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Reinforcement learning (RL), and also multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), is the algorithm used underneath for agents that interact with a dynamic environment and make decisions in it. In MARL there are multiple players (agents) that interact with the environment, and the environment dynamics depend on the joint actions of all of the agents. Researchers usually assume that MARL is a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and that the game model is a Markov game (MG). RL is used in a lot of different scenarios, for example autonomous driving, financial decisions, recommendation systems, and drones' and robots' algorithms. RL models, MARL included, are being used more and more in critical tasks, so understanding the security and adversarial robustness of RL and MARL is becoming more important.

Some recent works have looked at adversarial attacks on single-agent RL. In general there are 5 types of adversarial attacks: observation poisoning attacks, environment poisoning attacks, action-only poisoning attacks, reward-only poisoning attacks, and mixed poisoning attacks. For example, one work investigated the optimality of evasion attacks (attacks that reduce the expected total reward the agents gain) under a budget constraint, looking at it from the perspective of policy perturbations during learning. Another work proposed two types of attacks, the strategically-timed attack and the enchanting attack, where the attacker wants to lure the victim (recipient) agent into a designated target state.

For MARL, most of the existing works looked at a model where one limitless attacker attacks multiple agents. One work proposed a mediator model with a generalized mediator's objective, where the mediator (attacker) attacks the agents in the game to mediate them so that the objective function in an MG is maximized. Another work proposed adversarial attacks on the communication of multi-agent systems. The mediator work considers one limitless mediator (attacker) that attacks recipient agents. But in reality attacks are more likely to be done by distributed agents, and every attacker has a budget constraint on the resources it uses for attacks.

In this paper we propose a new formulation of adversarial attack in MARL, which is the agent-attack-agent model. In this model distributed agents perform the adversarial attacks instead of central mediators, each attack between an attacker and recipient pair has its own distinct cost, and each attacker is limited by its own attack budget. We propose an optimal method that integrates within-step static constrained attack-resource allocation optimization and between-step dynamic programming to get the optimal adversarial attack in multiple agent systems. Our numerical results show that the proposed attacks can reduce the rewards that the attacked agents receive by a lot.

The rest of the paper is organized like this. Section 2 introduces the agent-attack-agent model and formulates the problem of finding optimal attacks. Section 3 considers two budget constraint scenarios and proposes two corresponding optimal algorithms for finding the optimal attack policy. Section 4 numerically evaluates the performance of the proposed attack algorithms.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Reinforcement learning (RL), including multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), is used as the underlying algorithm for agents to interact with and make decisions in a dynamic environment. In MARL, multiple players (agents) interact with the environment, and the environment dynamics depend on the joint actions of all the agents. Researchers often assume that MARL is a Markov Decision Process (MDP) [1] and that the game model is a Markov game (MG) [2]. RL has many applications in different scenarios, for example autonomous driving [3], financial decisions [4], recommendation systems [5], and drones' and robots' algorithms [6]. Since RL models, including MARL, are increasingly used in critical tasks, understanding the security and adversarial robustness of RL and MARL is becoming more and more important.

Several recent works have addressed adversarial attacks of single-agent RL [7,8,9,10,11]. In general there are 5 types of adversarial attacks: observation poisoning attacks, environment poisoning attacks, action-only poisoning attacks, reward-only poisoning attacks, and mixed poisoning attacks [12,13,14,7,15,16]. For example, in [8], the authors investigated the optimality of evasion attacks (which reduce the expected total reward gained by agents) under a budget constraint from the perspective of policy perturbations during learning. In [9], the authors proposed two types of attacks, the strategically-timed attack and the enchanting attack, in which the attacker aims to lure the victim (recipient) agent into a designated target state.

For the MARL setting, most existing works investigated a model of one limitless attacker attacking multiple agents. In [13], with a generalized mediator's objective, the authors proposed a mediator model in which the mediator (attacker) attacks the agents in the game to mediate them to maximize the objective function in an MG. In [17], the authors proposed adversarial attacks on the communication of multi-agent systems. [13] considers one limitless mediator (attacker) attacking recipient agents. In reality, however, attacks are more likely to be performed by distributed agents, and every attacker has a budget constraint on the resources it uses for attacks.

In this paper, we propose a new formulation of adversarial attack in MARL, the agent-attack-agent model. In this model, distributed agents rather than central mediators perform adversarial attacks, each attack between an attacker and recipient pair has a distinct cost, and each attacker is limited by its own attack budget. We propose an optimal method that integrates within-step static constrained attack-resource allocation optimization and between-step dynamic programming to achieve the optimal adversarial attack in multiple agent systems. Our numerical results show that the proposed attacks can significantly reduce the rewards received by the attacked agents.

The rest of this paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we introduce the agent-attack-agent model and formulate the problem of finding optimal attacks. In Section 3, we consider two budget constraint scenarios and propose two corresponding optimal algorithms for finding the optimal attack policy. In Section 4, we numerically evaluate the performance of the proposed attack algorithms.
